extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys/agents) drafting or prosecuting U.S. patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on form, identification, examination, fee calculation, and incorporation-by-reference rules for dependent and multiple dependent claims in U.S. patent applications, including specification completeness and claim terminology requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification when referencing dependent claims (A/B/C)
rubrics_metrics.description: When making reference to a dependent claim either singular or multiple: (A) For a singular dependent claim which does not include a reference to a multiple dependent claim, reference only to the number of the dependent claim. (B) When identifying the embodiments included within a multiple dependent claim, or a singular dependent claim which includes a reference to a multiple dependent claim, each embodiment should be identified by using the number of the claims involved, starting with the highest, to the extent necessary to specifically identify each embodiment. (C) When all embodiments included within a multiple dependent claim or a singular dependent claim which includes a reference to a multiple dependent claim are subject to a common rejection, objection, or requirement, reference may be made only to the number of the dependent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes table/example showing allowed 'approved practice' identifications versus 'all claims' lists; if multiple dependent claim embodiments share a common ground of rejection, refer only to the dependent claim number (e.g., if 4/2 and 4/3 have common rejection, refer only to claim 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office actions must identify treatment for each claim embodiment (35 U.S.C. 132)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of 35 U.S.C. 132 require that each Office action make it explicitly clear what rejection, objection and/or requirement is applied to each claim embodiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple embodiments arise from multiple dependent claims, the examiner must explicitly state which rejection/objection applies to each embodiment; may use condensed references only when all embodiments share the same ground (see Identification rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form PTO/SB/07 for multiple dependent claim fee computation
rubrics_metrics.description: A separate 'Multiple Dependent Claim Fee Calculation Sheet,' form PTO/SB/07 is used with form PTO/SB/06 to assist in computation of fees for multiple dependent claims; OPAP places the form in the file when multiple dependent claims are present as filed or later added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple dependent claims are added later, TC technical support places form in file; totals from PTO/SB/07 are transferred to PTO/SB/06 for final fee calculation. This is an administrative requirement to compute fees correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper multiple dependent claim fee counting (definition of proper multiple dependent claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 41(a), claims in proper multiple dependent form may not be considered as single dependent claims for calculating fees; a multiple dependent claim is considered to be that number of dependent claims to which it refers. Any proper claim depending directly or indirectly from a multiple dependent claim is also considered as the number of dependent claims as referred to in the multiple dependent claim from which it depends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In fee calculations, a proper multiple dependent claim increases the dependent claim count by the number of claims it alternatively refers to; dependent claims that depend from a multiple dependent claim are counted accordingly (examples shown in fee calculation example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper multiple dependent claim treatment for fees and marking
rubrics_metrics.description: If none of the multiple dependent claims is proper, the multiple dependent claim fee is not required. However, if at least one multiple dependent claim is proper, the multiple dependent claim fee is required. If any multiple dependent claim is improper, OPAP may mark it by placing an encircled numeral '1' in the 'Dep. Claims' column of PTO/SB/07; the fee for any improper multiple dependent claim is only one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An improper multiple dependent claim (defective alternative form or depending on a prior multiple dependent claim) is counted as a single dependent claim for fee purposes and marked with encircled '1'; any claim depending from an improper multiple dependent claim is also considered improper and counted as one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial administrative acceptance of dependent claims for fee purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial determination for fee purposes as to whether a claim is dependent must be made by persons other than examiners; at that time, virtually every claim which refers to another claim is accepted as dependent without determining whether a true dependent relationship exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial acceptance as dependent for administrative fee counting does not preclude a later examiner determination that the claim is not a proper dependent claim for substantive examination; the examiner may subsequently hold a claim improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test for proper dependency under 35 U.S.C. 112(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 35 U.S.C. 112(d), a claim in dependent form shall contain: (i) a reference to a claim previously set forth, and (ii) then specify a further limitation of the subject matter claimed. A dependent claim is construed to incorporate by reference all the limitations of the claim to which it refers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dependent claim must include every limitation of the claim from which it depends and specify an additional limitation; omitting an element from the base claim (or replacing it) renders a dependent claim improper even if other limitations are added. The significance of the added limitation is not determinative; the requirement is formal: include all base limitations and add a further limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claims across statutory classes and separate inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: A dependent claim that relates to a separate invention that would require a separate search or separate classification from the base claim is not necessarily improper. The fact that independent and dependent claims are in different statutory classes does not, in itself, render the dependent claim improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a product claim may properly have a dependent method-of-making claim that further specifies limitations; conversely, a product claim would be improper as dependent on a method claim if the product can be made by methods other than that recited in the base method claim. Examiners must treat dependent claims as combinations (base limitations + dependent limitations) when comparing to prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination treatment for dependent claims that fail 35 U.S.C. 112(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a dependent claim does not comply with 35 U.S.C. 112(d), the examiner should reject the dependent claim under 35 U.S.C. 112(d) as unpatentable rather than merely objecting to the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs 7.36 (statutory basis) and then 7.36.01 (rejection wording). Form paragraph 7.36 should be used only once per Office action and must precede 7.36.01. Examiner notes instruct insertion of an explanation of why the dependent claim fails to constitute a further limitation and remind that non-compliance renders the claim unpatentable (citing Pfizer v. Ranbaxy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim form and arrangement rules for dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A singular dependent claim (e.g., 'The product of claim 1 in which . . .') is permissible. A series of singular dependent claims is allowed where each dependent claim refers to a preceding claim which in turn refers to another preceding claim. A claim which depends from a dependent claim should not be separated by any claim which does not also depend from said dependent claim. A dependent claim may refer back to any preceding independent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant's claim sequence should generally not be changed; examiners may advise using form paragraph 6.18. During prosecution the order may change, so check claim numbering and references carefully when claims are renumbered upon allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection/objection handling when base claim canceled or rejected
rubrics_metrics.description: If the base claim has been canceled, a claim which is directly or indirectly dependent thereon should be rejected as incomplete. If the base claim is rejected, the dependent claim should be objected to rather than rejected if it is otherwise allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.43 can be used to state the objection: 'Claim [1] objected to as being dependent upon a rejected base claim, but would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim terminology must have antecedent basis in description
rubrics_metrics.description: The meaning of every term used in the claims should be apparent from the descriptive portion of the specification with clear disclosure as to its import; in mechanical cases, refer to drawings/parts. New terminology introduced in claims (especially late in prosecution) should have clear support or antecedent basis in the specification so the meaning may be ascertained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid a confusing variety of terms for the same thing. When claims are amended or new claims added that introduce new terms, appropriate amendment of the specification is necessary (without introducing new matter) to provide clear support per 37 CFR 1.75(d)(1). If the specification fails to provide proper antecedent basis, use form paragraph 7.44 to object to the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of specification: written description, enablement, and utility requirements (35 U.S.C. 112)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application must include a specification containing a written description of the invention that enables a person skilled in the art to make and use the invention as of its filing date (35 U.S.C. 112). At least one specific operative embodiment or example must be set forth; examples and description should be of sufficient scope to justify the scope of the claims. The specification must reasonably convey possession of the claimed invention and enable it without undue experimentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complex experimentation is permitted if typical for the art; see additional MPEP sections for detailed guidance (e.g., enablement, written description, utility, computer-related claims, functional claims). For lack of utility or other specialized issues, consult referenced MPEP sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference general rule (37 CFR 1.57)
rubrics_metrics.description: An incorporation by reference in the specification must, except for limited reference-filing provisions, be set forth in the specification and must (1) express a clear intent to incorporate by reference by using the root words 'incorporat(e)' and 'reference', and (2) clearly identify the referenced patent, application, or publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (a) procedures apply for reference filing (applicable to certain post-2013 filings). A mere reference to material does not convey intent to incorporate; corrections to satisfy identification are permitted only when the material was sufficiently described to uniquely identify the document. Hyperlink or other browser-executable code incorporations are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential vs nonessential material for incorporation by reference (37 CFR 1.57(d)/(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Essential material (material necessary to provide written description/enablement, to particularly point out and distinctly claim the invention, or to describe structure/material/acts corresponding to a claimed means/step) may be incorporated by reference only to a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication that does not itself incorporate that essential material. Nonessential material may be incorporated by reference to U.S. or foreign patents or published applications, commonly owned U.S. applications, or non-patent publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential material is narrowly defined and cannot be incorporated by reference to foreign or non-patent sources for applications to issue as U.S. patents. An incorporation by hyperlink is not permitted. If incorporation is defective, the examiner may require applicant to supply a copy; insertion of incorporated material into the specification must be by amendment with a statement that no new matter is introduced. Corrections to incorporations must be made within Office-set time periods (no later than close of prosecution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and limitations when material is inadvertently omitted or added by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: If all or a portion of the specification or drawings is inadvertently omitted but is completely contained in a prior-filed application (priority or benefit claim present), the omission may be treated as incorporation by reference provided the omitted portion is later added within any office-set time (no later than close of prosecution) and certain documents/copies/translations and fees are supplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include supplying a copy of the prior-filed application, translations if needed, identifying where omitted portion is found, possible petition/fees if not entitled to filing date, and time limits for certified copies (e.g., within later of four months from filing date or sixteen months from previous filing date) unless petitioned. For international applications, special rules apply and additions may be effective only for the U.S. national stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner and Director discretion and policy on incorporation by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director has considerable discretion in determining what may be incorporated by reference in a patent application; the MPEP sets forth how that discretion is exercised for applications to issue as patents and for benefit/priority applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP guidance codifies practice (including 2004 and 2013 changes) limiting incorporation of essential material and providing procedures for reference filing under PLTIA; examiners should follow the delineated sections for applications to issue as patents (essential vs nonessential) and for benefit applications (see further MPEP sections referenced).
